title: Palm Beach Lakefront Estate Sells for $26.5M - 1,458% Above Its 2005 Price
summary: A lakefront house at 127 Ocean View Road in Palm Beach's Estate Section, about a mile south of Mar-a-Lago, traded for a recorded $26.5 million after more than 25 years in the same family. Heidi Niblack and retired pharmaceutical executive John Niblack sold as co-trustees of a revocable trust; the buyer was Florida Iconic Ventures LLC, managed by Issac Ashkenazy and sharing an address with New York-based Ashkenazy Acquisition Corp. The 1999-built, four-bedroom house has 8,387 square feet inside and out plus a lakefront pool and spa. The sellers paid $1.7 million in 2005 for the house and an oceanfront parcel down the street - a 1,458% gain.
source: Palm Beach Daily News via Boca Raton Tribune

title: Miami Beach Double-Lot Mansion Trades for $51.5M; Al Capone's Former Palm Island Lot Fetches $21M
summary: A trust paid $51.5 million for the newly built waterfront mansion at 270 South Hibiscus Drive in Miami Beach, off a $55 million ask. The seller was an entity managed by broker Denis Smykalov; the 10,500-square-foot, seven-bedroom house sits on a double lot. Jordan Karp had the listing and Dora Puig of Luxe Living Realty represented the buyer. Separately, the 30,000-square-foot waterfront lot at 93 Palm Avenue that once held Al Capone's mansion sold for $21 million to an LLC tied to Russian businessman Ilya Karpov, up from $15.5 million in 2021.

title: Brickell Development Site Sells for $50M for Planned 60-Story Tower; SW Miami-Dade Industrial Trades at $24.5M
summary: Prosper Group and Versluys Group paid $50 million for a Brickell assemblage - two commercial buildings totaling 16,800 square feet at 625 SW First Avenue and 66 SW Sixth Street plus a 74,400-square-foot vacant lot at 99 SW Seventh Street - from Two Roads Development and Newgard Development Group. The buyers are planning a 60-story residential tower on the site. In southwest Miami-Dade, a 155,000-square-foot two-story industrial building and parking lot at 11900-11905 SW 128th Street changed hands for $24.5 million.

title: Mortgage Rates Fall a Second Straight Week to 6.65%; 15-Year Dips to 5.95%
summary: Freddie Mac's Primary Mortgage Market Survey put the 30-year fixed at 6.65% for the week ending August 20, down from 6.67% and the second consecutive weekly decline. The 15-year fixed eased to 5.95% from 5.96%. Both sit modestly above year-ago levels of 6.58% and 5.69%. Jumbo 30-year pricing averaged roughly 6.78%, down from about 6.84% in mid-August - the more relevant benchmark for most South Florida coastal and luxury purchases, where loan sizes clear the $832,750 conforming ceiling.

title: Russian Businessman Sells Miami Beach's 2740 North Bay Road Lot for $72M, More Than Triple His 2022 Price
summary: Ilyha Karpov sold the vacant 0.6-acre waterfront lot at 2740 North Bay Road in Miami Beach to a trust for $72 million - the week's priciest recorded South Florida residential deal. Karpov had paid $20.8 million for the site in 2022, buying from Delphine Dray, owner of Miami Beach's National Hotel. The top commercial trade was in Miami Beach as well: an affiliate of Coral Gables-based Capital Realty Services sold the 31,000 SF two-story mixed-use building at 1200 Washington Avenue for $10 million, or about $323 per square foot, to an entity managed by investor Ryan Manoocheri; the property last traded for $2.8 million more than two decades ago. Also recorded: the estate of Rudolf Silk sold a 42,000 SF West Palm Beach industrial property at 2658-2660 Electronics Way for $7.8 million, and John Thomas Hayes paid $6.2 million for a 2022-built waterfront home at 3701 Northeast 26th Avenue in Lighthouse Point.

title: Kolter and Carlyle's 336-Unit One Alton Biscayne Tops Permits; Neumann's Flow and Huizenga File Demolitions
summary: For permits issued August 12-19, the largest was One Alton Biscayne, a 12-story, 336-unit apartment building at 11240 Biscayne Boulevard near North Miami from Kolter Multifamily, the Carlyle Group and Altman. The partners bought the site last year for $15 million and secured an $86.1 million construction loan from PNC Bank. On the demolition side, Huizenga Holdings - led by H. Wayne Huizenga Jr. - pulled seven permits across a West Palm Beach residential assemblage, Crescent Heights cleared the way for phase two of its 42-story Forma Suites tower in Miami's Edgewater, and Adam Neumann's Flow filed to demolish structures on the 16-acre former trailer park at 8500 Biscayne Boulevard it bought at a court-ordered auction for $70.5 million.

title: Palm Beach's 206 Phipps Plaza, a 1920s John Volk Design, Sells for $27.5M
summary: A company managed by Thomas J. Morrison sold the 6,900 SF house at 206 Phipps Plaza in Palm Beach to a trust for $27.5 million - the week's top recorded South Florida home sale. The seven-bedroom, nine-and-a-half-bath residence dates to the 1920s and once belonged to Palm Beach society architect John Volk; Jim McCann of Premier Estate Properties had the listing and Christopher Leavitt of Douglas Elliman represented the buyer. Also recorded that day: a 5,100 SF oceanfront home at 3567 South Ocean Boulevard in Highland Beach for $12.8 million - medical-technology executive Alexis Lukianov and his wife Katherine sold to Jonathan and Chemai Jura after first asking $15.9 million in October - plus a 5,000 SF villa at the Oceana Key Biscayne, 111 Reef Lane, for $10.9 million and a Miami Beach waterfront house at 5000 North Bay Road for $9.3 million.

title: U.S. Home-Sale Cancellations Hit Highest Level Since 2023; 14% of July Deals Fell Through
summary: Buyers backed out of just over 14 percent of pending U.S. home sales in July, the highest share since June 2023, according to Redfin data. More than 47,000 contracts were canceled nationwide during the month, a 4.8 percent year-over-year increase, though the cancellation share ran only 0.7 percentage points above July 2025. Southern markets, Florida among them, are posting the highest fall-through rates. The practical read for sellers: a signed contract is a weaker signal than it was two years ago - buyer diligence, insurance quotes and appraisal gaps are all live risks - so pricing to a realistic close rather than a headline list price matters more than it did in the 2021-22 market.

title: Bay Harbor Islands Waterfront Home Sells for $20M, Up from $12M in 2021
summary: Venture capitalist Fued Sadala and his wife Silvana sold their 5,900 SF waterfront home at 9814 West Broadview Drive in Bay Harbor Islands for $20 million - the week's top recorded South Florida home sale - to Jack Tabacinic, a managing director at Loom Capital Management, and Andrea Blau Russ. The 2002-built, five-bedroom house had been listed earlier in August at $22 million; the Sadalas paid $12 million for it in 2021, a roughly 67 percent gain in five years. Joel Lusky and Shneur Shapira of The Brokerage South Florida Real Estate represented both sides. Also recorded: a waterfront home at 4216 Intracoastal Drive in Highland Beach for $9.5 million, sold by hedge-fund manager Leonard Zelin and Moira Zelin to Antonio and Dolores Seabra, and a newly built home at 256 Alhambra Place in West Palm Beach for $7.5 million.

title: Florida Home Sales Rise for 11th Straight Month; Statewide Single-Family Median Hits $425,000
summary: July 2026 data released August 17 shows Florida's housing market posting its 11th consecutive month of year-over-year closed-sales gains in both major property types. Statewide single-family closings totaled 23,870, up 5.1%, while condo-townhouse sales totaled 8,194, up 11%. The statewide single-family median rose 3.7% to $425,000; the condo-townhouse median held flat at $295,000. Single-family inventory fell 13.4% to 97,741 active listings - a 4.5-months supply, squarely a seller's market - while condo supply sits at 7.8 months. Southeast Florida ran ahead of the state on price: Miami-Dade single-family median $685,000 (+3.8%), Broward $650,000 (+4.8%), Palm Beach $660,090 (+7.6%), with single-family active listings down 22.8%, 25.0% and 23.3% respectively. Million-dollar-plus sales climbed 15.5% in Miami-Dade and 33.9% in Broward.

title: Florida's November Property-Tax Amendment Draws Organized Opposition
summary: Amendment 3 on Florida's November ballot would raise the non-school homestead exemption from $50,000 to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 by 2028, and would cut the annual cap on assessment increases for non-homestead property from 10% to 5%. It needs 60% voter approval. Legislative fiscal analysis estimates local government revenue would fall roughly $4.6 billion in the first year and $8.4 billion in the second, with no funding mechanism specified. Three political committees organized to oppose it - including Vote No on 3, also called Stop Unfair Tax Shifts - have together raised under $30,000 since the start of June, arguing the measure shifts the burden onto renters, commercial property owners and first-time buyers. For income-property owners the line item to watch is the non-homestead assessment cap: dropping it to 5% would materially slow taxable-value growth on rentals and small commercial assets.

title: Artemis Pays $140M for Delray Beach Senior-Living Community; Golden Beach Oceanfront Lot Fetches $24M
summary: An entity tied to Chevy Chase, Maryland-based Artemis Real Estate Partners bought a senior-living community at 6589 and 6595 Morikami Park Road in Delray Beach for $140 million from an affiliate of PGIM Real Estate - among the largest assisted-living trades ever recorded in Florida and the week's priciest South Florida commercial sale. The 2023-built complex spans 225,000 SF on 7.2 acres and holds 207 residences: 70 assisted-living, 76 independent-living and 41 memory-care units, with average monthly resident rates around $7,635. The week's top recorded home sale was dirt, not a house: a 0.6-acre oceanfront lot at 625 Ocean Boulevard in Golden Beach traded for $24 million, sold by the estate of Sydell Herrick to a company managed by spec developer David Rodriguez, who plans to build on the site.

title: Ken Griffin Sells Palm Beach's 125 Worth Avenue to Blackstone Affiliate for $86M
summary: Citadel founder Ken Griffin sold his 50,000 SF office building at 125 Worth Avenue in Palm Beach to Blackstone's Revantage for $86 million - the week's priciest recorded South Florida commercial deal. Griffin had paid $83 million for the Worth Avenue property in 2023, and the resale underscores how tightly held - and how institutionally sought after - trophy office space on Palm Beach's premier retail corridor has become as financial firms continue relocating to the island. The week's second-largest commercial trade was industrial: a 120,700 SF warehouse at 16175 Northwest 49th Avenue in Hialeah sold for $31 million, or nearly $257 per square foot, with Kurv Industrial selling to an entity tied to Salt Lake City-based Alsco Uniforms after buying it for $26.3 million in 2022.

title: Miami Beach's 508 West Dilido Flips for $22.8M, Six Months After a $18.5M Purchase
summary: A 5,500 SF waterfront home at 508 West Dilido Drive on Miami Beach's Venetian Islands sold for $22.8 million - the week's top recorded South Florida home sale. The 508 W Dilido Drive Land Trust sold to the 508 Di Lido Land Trust after paying $18.5 million for the 2018-built house in February of this year, a roughly 23% gain in about six months. Reid Heidenry and Marko Gojanovic of One Sotheby's International Realty represented the seller and Hayley Dodge of Compass brought the buyer. Quick resales at a premium remain a recurring feature of the Venetian and Sunset Islands market, where finished new-construction inventory is scarce.

title: Rilea's $85.6M Mohawk at Wynwood Tops South Florida Construction Permits
summary: South Florida's largest construction permit for the week ending August 10 was an $85.6 million new-building permit for Mohawk at Wynwood, Rilea Group's 300-unit, 488,880 SF apartment project at 50 Northeast 29th Street in Miami, which will include 30,000 SF of ground-floor retail and deliver in 2028. Rilea, led by Alan and Diego Ojeda, bought the land for $22 million in 2021 and closed a $149.2 million construction loan in January that included $124.2 million of C-PACE financing from Nuveen Green Capital. Also permitted: a $31.1 million, 115,820 SF permit for Sweetbird North, an eight-story office-and-retail project at 95 Northeast 40th Street from Miami Design District Associates and Raycliff Capital, and a $28 million permit for Kolter Multifamily's 336-unit Alton Biscayne at 11240 Biscayne Boulevard in North Miami Beach.

title: Mortgage Rates Post First Drop in Six Weeks to 6.67%; 15-Yr Falls to 5.96%
summary: Freddie Mac's 30-year fixed-rate mortgage averaged 6.67% the week of August 13, down from 6.69% - its first weekly decline in six weeks - while the 15-year fixed fell to 5.96% from 6.01%. A year ago the 30-year FRM averaged 6.58%, leaving financing only marginally above year-ago levels. Chief economist Sam Khater said the modest pullback, combined with for-sale inventory that keeps improving and listing prices running slightly below a year ago, is gradually shifting conditions toward buyers. Bankrate/Mortgage Research Center pegged the 30-year jumbo average near 6.84% as of mid-August.
